Blender art spike: review

Ten assets from the current design, made by Claude with Blender scripts and rendered as toon sprites (the game is 2D Phaser). The agent's score sits next to each sheet. Record your own verdict below it. Choices save in this browser; Copy verdicts puts them on the clipboard as markdown to paste back to Claude.

  • Is this the Atelier look you want (pastel, chunky bevels, outlines, cute)? If not, the fix is in style_lib, not per asset.
  • Bottom row of each sheet = the real game camera at true phone size (DPR 3). Judge there first.
  • Does each asset read at that size: what it is, its role, its tier?
  • Do the assets look like one game when side by side (overview)?

Your verdict

Hero test: sprite camera angle

Left pair: medic at the game camera (48.6°) and at 15°. Right pair: the same for the Stone golem. At 48.6° you see the top of the head and lose the face; at 15° both read better. Units are upright billboard sprites, so the sprite angle can differ from the board tilt (as in Arknights). Decision for you: render unit sprites at about 15°?

Hero test: generated references (idle, then 3 action tries)

Independent generations drift in proportions, hair and outfit. Action stills should come from posing the idle 3D model (a rig), not from a second generation.

Hero test: idle and action stills as 3D

Idle at 48.6° and 15°, action at 48.6° and 15°, then idle and action at 3/4. The action still is recognisably the same character but noisier.

Overall

Go / no-go on this pipeline, and anything about the style itself
